Most likely the htmx request from the partial isn't carrying the CSRF token: Django needs it either as a hidden `csrfmiddlewaretoken` field in the posted form or in the `X-CSRFToken` header, and a token that only sits in the base template isn't sent with requests from inside the partial. The usual fixes are putting `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form in the partial, or setting `hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}'` on `<body>` in the base template so every htmx request gets it. I'd also confirm the CSRF cookie is actually set on that page.

A 403 CSRF failure after moving a form into a partial usually means the token is not reaching the htmx request. Common causes: the partial is rendered without the request (so `{% csrf_token %}` outputs nothing), the `{% csrf_token %}` tag was left outside the moved form, or the token was sent via an `hx-headers` attribute on an element that is no longer an ancestor of the form. A token in the base template only helps if the form or one of its parents carries it.
Action: Ask you to share the partial and the view that renders it, so I can check where the token ends up.
